note: Kalpa Labs' own plain-English wording. No ISO standard text is copied. IDs and short titles come from 06-finops/src/frameworks/iso42001-2023.json (Probo, MIT). Buy ISO/IEC 42001:2023 from ISO or BIS for the real requirements.

scale.1: Started or informal (talked about, not written down)
scale.2: Mostly in place, written down, some gaps
scale.3: In place, written, followed, with evidence
scale.na: Not applicable (Annex A only; give the reason, it goes in the Statement of Applicability)

4.title: Context
4.about: Know your business, who cares about your AI, and draw the boundary of what the AI management system covers.

5.title: Leadership
5.about: Top management owns AI governance, signs an AI policy and names who is responsible for what.

6.title: Planning
6.about: Decide how you find, rate and treat AI risks and impacts, and set measurable AI goals.

7.title: Support
7.about: People, skills, awareness, communication and controlled documents that keep the system running.

8.title: Operation
8.about: Actually run the risk assessments, treatments and impact assessments you planned, and control changes.

9.title: Performance evaluation
9.about: Measure how the system works, audit it internally and review it at management level.

10.title: Improvement
10.about: Fix what is broken, find root causes, and keep improving.

A.2.title: AI policies
A.2.about: A written AI policy that fits your other policies and is reviewed on a schedule.

A.3.title: Internal organisation
A.3.about: Clear AI roles and a safe way for staff to raise concerns.

A.4.title: Resources for AI systems
A.4.about: A record of the data, tools, compute and people each AI system depends on.

A.5.title: Impact assessment
A.5.about: A repeatable way to judge how each AI system can affect people, groups and society, kept on file.

A.6.title: AI system life cycle
A.6.about: Responsible design, testing, release, monitoring, documentation and logging across the life of each AI system.

A.7.title: Data for AI systems
A.7.about: Know where AI data comes from, how good it is and how it was prepared.

A.8.title: Information for interested parties
A.8.about: Tell users and others what they need to know, report externally where needed, and communicate incidents.

A.9.title: Use of AI systems
A.9.about: Rules and goals for responsible use, and each system used only for its intended purpose.

A.10.title: Third parties and customers
A.10.about: Split responsibilities with suppliers and customers, and check AI suppliers.

questions.4.1: Have you written down the internal and external issues (business, legal, tech, social) that affect your AI work?
questions.4.2: Do you have a list of people and groups affected by your AI (customers, staff, regulators) and what they expect?
questions.4.3: Is there a written scope saying which AI systems, teams and sites the management system covers?
questions.4.4: Is the AI management system set up as a working set of processes, not just documents?
questions.5.1: Does a named senior leader actively back AI governance with time, budget and attention?
questions.5.2: Is there an approved AI policy that states your aims and commitments for responsible AI?
questions.5.3: Are AI roles (owner, risk, review, approval) assigned to named people and known to them?
questions.6.1.1: Have you decided how you will find and handle risks and opportunities of the AI management system?
questions.6.1.2: Is there a written method to identify, analyse and rate AI risks with clear criteria?
questions.6.1.3: Is there a method to choose and track risk treatments, with an owner and due date per risk?
questions.6.1.4: Is there a method to assess how an AI system may affect people and society before release?
questions.6.2: Are there measurable AI objectives with owners, resources and deadlines?
questions.6.3: Are changes to the AI management system planned and controlled, not ad hoc?
questions.7.1: Are enough people, money and tools set aside to run AI governance?
questions.7.2: Do people in AI roles have the skills needed, and is that recorded (training, experience)?
questions.7.3: Do staff know the AI policy, their part in it and what happens if they ignore it?
questions.7.4: Is it decided what to communicate about AI, to whom, when and by whom?
questions.7.5.1: Do you keep the documents the system needs and that you decided are necessary?
questions.7.5.2: Do documents have a title, owner, version, date and review before use?
questions.7.5.3: Are documents stored safely, access-controlled, versioned and kept for a set period?
questions.8.1: Are AI processes planned, run to agreed criteria, and outsourced parts controlled?
questions.8.2: Are AI risk assessments actually carried out on schedule and when things change, with results kept?
questions.8.3: Are the chosen risk treatments put in place and their results recorded?
questions.8.4: Are AI impact assessments carried out on schedule and on major change, with results kept?
questions.9.1: Do you measure how well AI governance and AI systems perform, with set metrics and frequency?
questions.9.2.1: Do you run internal audits of the AI management system at planned times?
questions.9.2.2: Is there an audit plan (scope, frequency, auditors who do not audit their own work) and are results reported?
questions.9.3.1: Does top management review the AI management system at planned intervals?
questions.9.3.2: Do those reviews cover audit results, risks, objectives, incidents and feedback?
questions.9.3.3: Do reviews end with recorded decisions and actions?
questions.10.1: Is there a habit of improving the AI management system, with examples?
questions.10.2: When something goes wrong, do you fix it, find the root cause, act and record it?
questions.A.2.2: Is there a documented AI policy for developing or using AI systems?
questions.A.2.3: Has the AI policy been checked against your security, privacy, quality and HR policies?
questions.A.2.4: Is the AI policy reviewed on a set schedule and after big changes?
questions.A.3.2: Are AI roles and duties defined across the AI life cycle?
questions.A.3.3: Can staff raise AI concerns safely (named channel, no retaliation, follow-up)?
questions.A.4.2: Is there a list of resources each AI system needs (an AI system inventory)?
questions.A.4.3: Are the data resources for each AI system recorded (source, type, personal data or not)?
questions.A.4.4: Are the tools (models, APIs, libraries, platforms) for each AI system recorded?
questions.A.4.5: Are compute and hosting resources for each AI system recorded?
questions.A.4.6: Are the people and skills each AI system depends on recorded?
questions.A.5.2: Is there a process to assess the impact of AI systems on people and society?
questions.A.5.3: Are impact assessment results documented and kept?
questions.A.5.4: Do assessments consider effects on individuals and groups (fairness, safety, privacy, children)?
questions.A.5.5: Do assessments consider wider societal effects?
questions.A.6.1.2: Are there written goals for responsible AI development (e.g. fairness, transparency, safety)?
questions.A.6.1.3: Are there processes for responsible design and development (reviews, sign-offs)?
questions.A.6.2.2: Are requirements for each new AI system or major change written down before building?
questions.A.6.2.3: Are design and development decisions documented?
questions.A.6.2.4: Are AI systems tested and validated against set criteria before release (incl. prompt-injection tests)?
questions.A.6.2.5: Is there a release plan and approval before an AI system goes live?
questions.A.6.2.6: Are live AI systems monitored (errors, drift, misuse, cost) with someone acting on alerts?
questions.A.6.2.7: Is technical documentation available for the users and teams who need it?
questions.A.6.2.8: Are AI event logs recorded and kept for a set period?
questions.A.7.2: Is data management defined for developing and improving AI systems?
questions.A.7.3: Is it recorded how and from where AI data is acquired, and on what terms?
questions.A.7.4: Are data quality requirements set and checked?
questions.A.7.5: Is data provenance (origin and changes) recorded?
questions.A.7.6: Are data preparation steps (cleaning, labelling, PII removal) defined and recorded?
questions.A.8.2: Do users get the information they need about the AI system (what it is, limits, how to get help)?
questions.A.8.3: Can interested parties report adverse impacts, and is external reporting handled?
questions.A.8.4: Is there a plan to tell users and others about AI incidents?
questions.A.8.5: Is it decided what you must tell interested parties and is that information kept up to date?
questions.A.9.2: Are there processes for responsible use of AI systems by staff and customers?
questions.A.9.3: Are there written goals for responsible use?
questions.A.9.4: Is each AI system used only for its documented intended use?
questions.A.10.2: Are AI responsibilities split clearly between you, suppliers, partners and customers?
questions.A.10.3: Are AI suppliers (model and API providers) checked and do contracts cover your needs?
questions.A.10.4: Do you consider customer needs and expectations when providing AI products?
